extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners and KIPO staff responsible for examination, classification, and processing of patent/utility-model applications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards that KIPO examiners must follow for document formality, IPC assignment, publication (laying open), requests and start of examination, deferral rules, processing deadlines, law application, and prior-art search strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grade of examiner — qualification and promotion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Grade of examiner is decided in accordance with experience in patent examination, assessment of examination performance, completion of required training program for each level; chief examiner >10 years experience, senior examiner >7 years, junior examiner >4 years plus completion of training courses (Article 5-7 of Instruction on Operation of Patent Examiner Grade System).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision made by advancement deliberation committee in KIPO; experience, performance, and training completion are decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and naming of examination-related documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If KIPO determines a due form for certain documents, use that form; absent a designated form, use a general document form per Instruction on Office Management. If documents are attached, list attachments at end of document body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent examination documents shall be conducted in the name of the examiner in charge except for certain specified matters (e.g., Article 46 amendment requests, Article 16 invalidation measures, Article 11 returns, accelerated examination). Joint or consultative examinations carry joint names of all examiners concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC assignment must be accurate and based on scope of claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: IPC assignment must be made accurately based on the scope of the invention since it is necessary for effective search and retrieval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification impacts search effectiveness for IP offices and users; ensure assignments reflect true scope of claimed subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary basis for classification: claimed invention scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical subject-matter in the claims should be classified into IPC symbols (section, class, subclass, main group, subgroup) and classification shall be made on the basis of the scope of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the scope of the invention is unclear, use the detailed description (and drawings if necessary); technical subject-matter only in the description can be an additional basis for classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main vs. sub-classification when multiple technical subject-matters exist
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple technical subject-matters are involved, the core technical subject-matter representing the claimed invention as a whole is 'main classification', others are 'sub-classification'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hard to separate, use claim 1 (the first claim) as basis for classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification must reflect essential contents of claimed invention as a whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine classification based on the essential contents of the claimed invention as a whole without regard to the category of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an electronic radio circuit with tuner/demodulator/amplifier/output is classified as the whole circuit unless core subject-matter concerns a specific part; then classify by that part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion to grant additional information (indexing codes and symbols)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is discretionary to grant additional information for already classified invention via indexing codes or classification symbols; main classification should have attributes of invention information (I) while indexing code has attributes of additional information (N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical matter not in claims but in description/drawings may be assigned a classification symbol for additional information; method of granting applies mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of unity rule for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where lack of unity exists, the subject-matter stated in claim 1 becomes main classification while the place for other claims becomes sub-classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure unity considerations are reflected in main/sub assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and public-policy considerations in classification/publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If claimed invention requires confidentiality due to national security, contravenes public order/morality, or injures public health, or relates to convergence technologies, such requirement/concern must be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These considerations affect whether an application is laid open/published and must be flagged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve parent application classification for divisional/converted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For divisional, converted, domestic priority claim, or application by lawful holder, the classification of an earlier application should be identified first and preferably retained as the main classification of the subsequent application unless obviously inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New classifications can be designated as subclassification when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC assignment for apparatus vs. method — fallback hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, use classification place for either apparatus or method if a pertinent place exists; if apparatus has no place, use method place; if method has no place, use apparatus that performs the method; if neither exists, use place for product manufactured by apparatus/method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply fallback rules to find the best fitting IPC place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Products classification: product place, function, or areas of use
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufactured products shall be classified at the place pertinent to the product; if none, use appropriate function-oriented place; if none, use areas that use the product. If field of use is essential, classify by use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the most relevant place reflecting intrinsic product characteristics or essential use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multistage processes/compositions classification
rubrics_metrics.description: A multistage process or plant (process with multiple stages or a composition with multiple apparatuses) shall be classified at the place pertinent to the composition; if none, use place for output produced by the composition. Constituents with individual characteristics should also be classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If composition has no intrinsic characteristics but constituents do, do not classify the composition per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific/structural parts classification rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If structural/functional specifics or parts are used only for a certain apparatus, classify into the place for that apparatus; but if such parts can be used for more than two apparatus, classify in place for those specifics/parts. If no place exists, classify in place for relevant apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer parts classification when reuse across multiple apparatuses is broad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single technical subject related to multiple groups
rubrics_metrics.description: If a single technical subject matter is related to more than two groups directly and intrinsically, classify in the place for all related groups. If included in more than two equal-level groups under same main group, classify in place for higher hierarchic group unless inclusion into multiple groups is of little importance for search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subject relates to several groups under different main groups, classify for each group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compounds classification (including when field of use is essential)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical compounds (organic, inorganic, polymer) shall be classified in Section C according to intrinsic chemical-structure characteristics; if field of use is essential content, classify in place for field of use when pertinent place exists; if invention relates to use of compound, classify only the field of use if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify by intrinsic chemical features first; use-of-compound claims may change classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixtures and compositions classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixtures or compositions shall be classified pursuant to intrinsic features (e.g., glass composition C03C, cement C04B, alloy C22C). If no relevant place, classify pursuant to use or application; if essential characteristics exist in use, classify both the mixture/composition and their application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer intrinsic-feature-based places; fallback to use/application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of manufacture or treatment of compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: When claimed invention concerns manufacture/treatment of compounds, classify the compounds per se provided relevant place exists; methods of manufacture/treatment shall also be classified if pertinent places exist. General methods classify where relevant place exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both product and method classifications when meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush-type compounds classification
rubrics_metrics.description: For Markush-type compounds (general chemical formula), classify the general formula individually if the formula has few relevant places (e.g., less than 5). Specified compounds that are things per se, outputs, or derivatives should be classified in each relevant place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified means 'designated' by structure/formula, 'inferred' from manufacturing method, or 'identified' by physical properties or detailed examples; classify these as useful search information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinatorial-library compounds classification
rubrics_metrics.description: For combinatorial libraries with many different compounds, classify each individual compound as per Markush-type rules; characteristics of the entire library should be classified under combinatorial chemistry (C40B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the library as both aggregate (C40B) and as individual compound entries where useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation of IPC — examiner's verification of pre-classification
rubrics_metrics.description: When pre-classification is assigned by an outsourcing agency, the examiner must check whether pre-classification was appropriate based on claim subject-matter with reference to description/drawings and reclassify if incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reclassification by examiner is allowed; follow hierarchical IPC path from high to low level when determining classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official confirmation and reallocation for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: After pre-classification is verified or reclassified, the examiner in charge confirms it as 'official classification'. If further classification requires consultation, re-allocate to another examiner and confirm by mutual agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receiving examiner shall 'confirm' the classification once mutually agreed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification adjustment between divisions — escalation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If different examination divisions are involved or if mutual agreement between examiners fails, request classification adjustment stating reasons; if still disputed, involve Bureau classification officer(s) and then officers in Examination Bureau/Division to reach agreement under pre-classification review officer initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow hierarchical dispute resolution within KIPO classification officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for classification confirmation/reclassification requests
rubrics_metrics.description: For accelerated examination requests and applications requiring an international search, classification confirmation or reclassification request shall be made within 2 weeks from application transfer/receipt. For other applications this time limit may be extended by 1 month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure prompt classification processing for time-sensitive categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of laying open (publication) of application
rubrics_metrics.description: Laying open scheme (publication after a prescribed period from filing) prevents overlaps in investment and research by making application contents publicly available even if examination is pending; separates publication from examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication makes inventions part of common knowledge and supports social/industrial use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of laying open — general rule and priority handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are laid open more than one year and six months after filing date. For priority-claim applications, publication time is reckoned from either filing date of initial application in other country or filing date of earlier application (or earliest filing date when multiple priorities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional or converted applications receive same filing date as parent; early publication requests can move laying-open earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional/converted application laying-open rules relative to parent
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional/converted applications have time for laying open reckoned from parent filing date; if filed before parent publication, they are laid open later than 1.5 years from parent filing; if filed after parent publication, laid open without delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand relationship between parent and divisional filing dates for publication scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early publication request option
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may submit an early publication request form (specified form in Enforcement Rules) to have the application laid open within one year and six months from filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prescribed form to expedite publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content scope and exceptions for laying open
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle all patent applications shall be laid open after 1.5 years unless excluded: applications omitting statement of scope of claims (Article 42(5)), applications whose registration is published, or applications invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Article 19(3) of Enforcement Decree for matters to be laid open and statutory exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-disclosure for national security/public order/public health concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application shall not be disclosed in patent gazette if it contains matters requiring confidentiality due to national security, or is liable to contravene public order/morality or to injure public health (Patent Act Article 64, Enforcement Decree Article 19(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag sensitive content to prevent publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form/medium of laying open
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are laid open in the online patent gazette on the KIPO website; same publication may appear on DVD-ROM and via KIPI website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use official KIPO publication channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of laying open — provisional rights and prior-art status
rubrics_metrics.description: After laying open, applicant may give written warning and later demand compensation from a person who worked the invention as a business after warning or after person knew of the laid-open application, but right to demand compensation cannot be exercised until registration; laying-open also makes claimed invention prior art under Article 29(1) subparagraphs (i) and (ii) and usable for other applications under Article 29(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laying open creates both procedural consequences (compensation pathway post-registration) and substantive prior-art effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination — general eligibility and single-request rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for examination shall be filed only for an application pending in KIPO; request is allowed only once per application, cannot be withdrawn, and continues despite loss of legal capacity (e.g., death). For requests by applicant, description with scope of claims must be attached to written application (Article 59(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure attachments meet statutory requirements; a single, irrevocable request starts substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may request examination, including third parties without interest; incompetents (e.g., minors) must appoint legal representatives; associations/foundations without juridical person status but with designated rep may file a request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad standing to request examination; procedural representation required where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to file request for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for examination shall be filed within five years from filing date for patents (three years for utility models). For divisional or converted applications, a person may request within thirty days from filing date of divisional/converted application even after the five-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to request within prescribed period results in deemed withdrawal of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to file request — form and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: File written request (specified form in Enforcement Rules) to Commissioner of KIPO and pay examination fee. If number of claims increases due to amendments after others' request, applicant must pay additional fee for increased claims; failure to pay may invalidate the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely payment and correct form are required; monitor claim-count fee implications on amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of filing request for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications with a valid examination request will be examined and can be terminated only by patent registration or rejection (unless invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned). When request is made before laying open, the purpose of the request is published upon publication; applicants must amend specifications omitting claim scope when notified by third-party request; Commissioner must notify applicant if request was filed by third party and notify third party of final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand procedural notifications and amendment obligations triggered by third-party requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of examination — allocation verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner must verify whether the application is appropriately allocated in terms of IPC and validity of his/her function; this verification should be concluded quickly to prevent delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check IPC scope alignment and examiner exclusion/ineligibility before beginning substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner exclusion checks before examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall review whether he/she falls under exclusion reasons in Article 148 (i)-(v),(vii) or is excluded because they had less than 2 years' examiner experience but served at the organization filing the application in the last 3 years before appointment; if exclusion exists, reassign application to another examiner with similar technical classification with director approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect impartiality/conflict-of-interest by reallocation when exclusion reasons apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of examination start and priority rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination starts in order of the request for examination by category of examiner or classification (subclass). If request dates identical by category/classification, patent application has priority over utility model; if same kind, earlier filing date has priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow defined ordering to determine queueing of examinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional/converted application examination order relative to parent
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional/converted applications are examined in order of their examination request, but examination may start in order of parent's request when filed after parent's request; if parent is divided/converted after examination started, examination of divisional starts before the later date of either 3 months from divisional request or 2 months from receipt of application documents. Divisional of accelerated parent follows parent's order rather than above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply special rules to coordinate parent/divisional examination timing, with special handling for accelerated parent cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for deferring examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may defer examination where: (i) earlier or competitive application is not laid open or competitive app not on examination request, (ii) earlier domestic priority claim is prior to withdrawal period under Article 56, (iii) related trial/litigation pending, (iv) search outsourced or outside specialist advice requested or consultation required, (v) period for submitting priority evidence under treaty not elapsed, (vi) other arising needs for deferral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferral is permitted when there are procedural or investigatory reasons beyond examiner's control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral procedure and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When deferring, examiner must report to head of examination unit and the deferral period is less than 2 months; if further deferral needed, report to head of division/team. Reasons (iv) and (vi) apply only when examiner cannot take responsibility (e.g., delivery delay of prior-art search report). Examiner can defer again within 2 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferrals require supervisory notification and generally short duration; track and report reasons for repeated deferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic check of deferral reasons and resumption requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall check whether deferral reasons are overcome for deferred applications at least once a month; when reasons are overcome, the examiner shall resume examination until deferral period terminates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly reviews ensure deferral does not linger unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple applications claiming identical invention
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more applications claim identical invention, examination of later applications shall be deferred until the earlier application is processed/laidoff/registered in patent gazette. If both applications can be rejected by the same reason, examination may begin without deferral. Final decision for later application made after confirming claim scope in earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate examination to preserve priority and avoid conflicting grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing deadlines and statutory/administrative timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Various processing deadlines are prescribed (e.g., reexamination should begin within 1 month of document receipt for returned/cancelled cases; accelerated-exam category decision within 7 days of request receipt; examination begin within 2 months from delivery of notice; interim documents processed within specified months/days). A detailed table defines deadlines for IPC classification, examination start, interim documents, accelerated/super-accelerated timelines, prior-art search request responses, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the table of reference times (months/weeks/days) for each type of action; examples: reexamination start: 1 month; accelerated decision: 7 days; expiration of amendment periods often 1 month or specified days depending on accelerated/super-accelerated categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principle for law application to pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When Patent Act revision occurs while an application is pending, transitional measures apply to prevent disadvantages; provisions of law are applied as of the filing date. Divisional/converted applications and those by lawful right holders are accorded the parent filing date so provisions are applied as of parent filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For priority/domestic priority/claims of not-prejudicial disclosures, apply law as of original application filing date; use examples to determine applicable law when revisions occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of search for prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for prior art is performed during examination to discover relevant state of the art to assess patentability (novelty and inventive step), including search for earlier applications per Article 36 and Article 29(3); examiner may outsource search to specialized organizations pursuant to Article 58(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search outcomes support substantive novelty/inventive-step determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-search procedure: analyze technical subject-matter and cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Before searching, examiner shall analyze technical subject-matters of the invention; search should be based on the claims but consider detailed description/drawings if necessary. When application cites documents, analyze whether they provide starting point, show current technology status, explain other solutions, or aid understanding; disregard irrelevant cited documents. If necessary documents cannot be acquired, request submission from applicant and defer examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cited documents as starting points when relevant; obtain necessary documents by request and defer if they are essential and unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of foreign patent office/search organization outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: If foreign patent offices or search organizations have conducted searches regarding the claimed invention, the examiner shall review those outcomes to determine whether they can be used as relevant prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage prior searching by other offices as appropriate but verify relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search procedure: collections, scope and strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Search is carried out in systematically accessible document collections/databases — primarily patent documents supplemented by technical journals, periodicals, books, microfiche, CD-ROM, DVD-ROM. Search strategy should determine documentation sections covering directly relevant technical fields and may extend to analogous fields as judged case-by-case based on initial search outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor search breadth to the invention and emerging results; exercise examiner judgment in extending search to analogous fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search may be limited or not required in certain cases
rubrics_metrics.description: No special search effort is required or search may be limited if the claimed invention falls under certain cases (enumeration continues beyond this chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should apply listed conditions to decide when exhaustive search is unnecessary; check the full guidelines for specific cases.
